text:
Evgeni Malkin is 40, in his 21st season with the only NHL team he has known, and still producing like a top-six forward: 16 points in 16 games, three assists in a win in Los Angeles on Nov. 7, and a turn on the wing beside Sidney Crosby. The story around him is not his play. Pittsburgh is losing, and the trade talk has started; reporters are openly asking what happens to Malkin if the Penguins sell before the January deadline.

His game has the shape it has had for years. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 96th percentile of forwards as a setup man last season, with 55% of his shots off the rush. Evolving-Hockey had his team creating a lot more with him on, and giving up a lot more too (bottom 4% of forwards defensively). He is shooting 17.6%, a bit above his range, so a few goals may slip.

What to watch: his minutes, which have dipped a minute a night lately, and the phone in Pittsburgh's front office.
headline: Malkin at 40, on a team heading for a sale
